Designed by Ohara Shōson (小原祥邨, 1877–1945)—also known as Ohara Koson—and published by Watanabe Shōzaburō in 1927, Cockatoo and Pomegranate (Zakuro ni Ōmu) is a celebrated masterpiece of the Shin-hanga bird-and-flower genre (kachō-ga).

Set against a deep, jet-black background that dramatically isolates the subject, a pristine white cockatoo perches gracefully on a textured, mossy branch with one dark claw tucked up against its chest plumage. Beside the bird rests a ripe, burst-open pomegranate showing its jewel-like white seeds inside, balanced by rich green foliage and delicate crimson buds. Shōson masterfully employs subtle blind printing/embossing (kara-zuri) to give tactile volume and softness to the cockatoo’s feathers, creating a striking contrast against the dark background. The bottom right corner features the artist’s signature ("Shōson") alongside his circular red artist seal.
